result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would ensure that every person has access to quality education—regardless of their background, location, gender, or socioeconomic status.

Education is foundational: it empowers individuals to think critically, solve problems, make informed choices, and contribute meaningfully to society. It’s linked to better health outcomes, economic opportunity, gender equality, and social cohesion. When people are educated, they’re more likely to lift themselves and their communities out of poverty, participate in democratic processes, and drive innovation.

Unlike many changes that address symptoms, universal access to quality education tackles root causes of inequality and injustice. It’s a ripple effect—empowering one generation transforms the next.

Of course, achieving this would require immense global cooperation, investment, and cultural shifts—but if it were possible with a single change, this is the one I’d choose.
